--- title: Throwback Thursday XSLT date: 2026-11-09 --- Hello from **2008**! (ish)
A 2026 lark: blogtini, but 2008 style -- before browsers drop XSLT (Chrome ~155; Firefox & Safari too).
This page is [XML](https://github.com/traceypooh/blogtini/blob/main/2026-11-throwback-thursday/xslt/index.xml). The browser runs [shell.xsl](shell.xsl) on it, which paints an HTML shell w/ the markdown in a `<pre>` & a `<script>` tag. The script runs it all through showdown.
Content is in a CDATA block (so `<` & `&` needn't be escaped) - -- the browser runs it on this file => an HTML shell: the text in a `<pre>` + `<script src=loader.js>` - [loader.js](loader.js) -- front matter via js-yaml, markdown via showdown (same pins as `index.js`), swaps out the `<pre>`
Notes: - no build - one stylesheet - fail open - no JS => the raw markdown in a `<pre>` - no XSLT => polyfill fallback or else the browser's XML tree view / text - crawlers mostly don't run XSLT -- not for real sites. blogtini's `index.html` posts do the same job w/ the HTML parser
> Party like it's [XSLT 1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/xslt-10/).
